title: fix(app-shell): Studio's app designer canvas shows a locale-map nav label and renames only the current locale's entry (objectui#11128)
body:
Fixes #11128
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/AppNavCanvas.tsx`, the design-mode nav editor used by the app preview and by the Studio app pillar. The spec types a nav item's `label` as `I18nLabel`: a plain string or an inline locale map.

- **Display.** `navLabel` now resolves the label in the designer locale through the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` (the resolver `AppPreview` already uses). A map-labelled entry no longer reads as the positional "Item 1" while the preview's landing line beside it shows the resolved text.
- **Rename.** The inline rename no longer writes the typed text over a whole map. A new `renamedLabel` helper keeps a plain string (or an absent label) as a plain string, as before. For a map it writes only the designer locale's entry and keeps every other entry. The entry written is the one `resolveI18nLabel` reads first for that locale: the exact tag, else its bare language. A map with neither gains an entry under the exact designer tag. An entry that the resolver only reached as another language's fallback (`default`, `en` under `zh-CN`, a sibling region such as `zh-TW`) is left as it was.
- **Fallback.** "Item N" stays only for a label that is truly absent or resolves to nothing. It now reads a designer catalogue row, `engine.appNav.item`, through the same `tFormat` and locale. The en value `Item {n}` renders byte-equal to the old text; zh is `导航项 {n}`.
- The locale is threaded from the canvas's own `useMetadataLocale()` into the card tree as a prop. The card's draft effect now keys on the resolved label string instead of the item object.

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`: the one `engine.appNav.item` row in the en and zh tables. `.changeset/11128-app-nav-canvas-label-maps.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

## Pins

New file `previews/AppNavCanvas.labelMaps-11128.test.tsx`, 7 tests. Each one renders `AppPreview` in design mode inside an `I18nProvider`, with the preview `locale` set to match:

- a map-labelled item shows `Accounts` under en and `客户` under zh, with no positional fallback and no `[object Object]`;
- an unlabelled item under zh shows the zh `engine.appNav.item` row, which differs from the en row;
- a rename under zh writes `{ en: 'Accounts', 'zh-CN': '客户账户' }`, so `en` survives;
- a rename under en writes the `en` entry the card read, `{ en: 'Customers', 'zh-CN': '客户' }`, with no second `en-US` key;
- a map with no entry for the designer locale gains one (`zh-CN`), and `default`, `en` and `zh-TW` are kept;
- a plain-string label renames to a plain string (the control).

## Verification (final commit `9d2fb10d8`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/studio-locale.i18n.test.tsx packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/`: `Test Files  151 passed (151)`, `Tests  1481 passed (1481)`.
- The closure was built first with `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (exit 0). Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check --listFiles` ran `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles`, exit 0, and the test project's file list includes the new pin file.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three changed source files: 3 files, 0 errors, 2 warnings. Both warnings are already there at base `9fd6c2c6f`, on the same statements with the same rules (`no-explicit-any` on the draft read, `set-state-in-effect` on the draft reset). The eslint config has no type-aware linting (no `projectService` or `parserOptions.project`) and no cross-file plugin, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- Gate verdicts, all exit 0: `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `pnpm check:i18n-designer-parity` ("every shared row carries the same placeholders"), `pnpm check:i18n-drift` (0 en values changed, 1 designer key added), `pnpm check:i18n-keys`, `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys` (the new key is not listed).
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four changed paths reports NOT GOVERNED.

**Ablations.** These were one-shot, run after the fix was committed. Restore was proved each time by the file's blob equalling the HEAD blob and by `git diff HEAD` being empty. Mutations 2 and 3 went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, and each anchor hit exactly once.

1. `AppNavCanvas.tsx` reverted whole to base `9fd6c2c6f`: `6 failed | 1 passed (7)`. Only the plain-string control stays green.
2. Only the rename write reverted to `label: nextLabel`, with the display fix kept: `3 failed | 4 passed (7)`. Each of the three map-rename pins receives a plain string.
3. The key picker reduced to "always the exact tag": `1 failed | 6 passed (7)`. The en pin receives `{ en: 'Accounts', 'en-US': 'Customers', 'zh-CN': '客户' }`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, reported to the seat and not changed here.** `StudioNavItemInspector` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) is the Studio app pillar's nav-item inspector beside this canvas. It reads the label as `String(node.label ?? node.title ?? node.name ?? '')`. I ran a probe that was not committed and was deleted afterwards: it rendered the inspector with `label: { en: 'Accounts', 'zh-CN': '客户' }`. The Label input showed `"[object Object]"`, and one keystroke wrote the plain string `"Customers"` over the whole map. So the inspector can still delete map text that this canvas now keeps. It is in the same family as this card, but it is not on this card's file surface.
- **The designer locale is `en-US` or `zh-CN`** (`useMetadataLocale`), not `en`. That is why the rename matches the exact tag, then the bare language: a `{ en, zh-CN }` map renamed in the English designer updates `en` instead of gaining an `en-US` key. The one remaining choice is which key a gained entry uses in the English designer. This PR uses `en-US`, the designer's own tag. It is raised with the seat as a question and does not block this PR.
- **The catalogue row's hole is spelled `{n}`**, the `tFormat` convention this table uses (as in `engine.inspector.widget.untitledN`). The carrier note's example spelling `Item {{n}}` would render `Item {1}` through `tFormat`.
